headline: Britain Joins Ukraine’s Avengers Labs
deck: Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Andy Burnham signed a joint declaration of intent in Kyiv on 24 August. The accompanying UK release says the deal will enable access to Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs database. The declaration itself does not create legally binding obligations. Ukraine’s standing rules still bar extraction of the corpus.
body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on a UK–Ukraine artificial-intelligence partnership in Kyiv on 24 August [E1]. The text commits the governments to co-developed models, secure data and compute pathways, and joint assurance, and to develop, test and deploy AI-enabled capabilities [E1]. It also says the declaration does not create legally binding obligations, and that further arrangements will be brought forward within the next few months [E1].

The more dramatic line sits in the accompanying UK implementation note, not in the declaration’s operative clauses. London said the partnership would enable access to Ukraine’s Avengers AI Labs database [E2]. Avengers, inside the DELTA ecosystem, is Ukraine’s automatic target-detection platform. Avengers Labs is the controlled environment built around annotated battlefield frames [E3]. The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine has published an annotated dataset of 5 million frames collected on the battlefield, most of them from DELTA, and says the trained system processes more than 100,000 UAV video streams a month [E3].

Access is not a download. Ukraine’s published Labs programme describes secure training of models without direct access to sensitive databases [E3]. No UK annex naming authorised institutions, egress rules or audit has been published [E1][E2]. Germany already signed a defence-data memorandum in April. Britain’s narrower claim is first partner into Avengers Labs, not first partner onto Ukrainian combat data [E2][E3].

A same-day SCALP announcement is adjacent, not this treaty. London said MBDA may release classified information on UK components so France and Ukraine can move toward local assembly [E2]. That is a separate information-release decision. Whether a named UK system is evaluated on Avengers Labs data by 30 November is the next public test [E1][E2][E3].

enable access to Ukraine’s coveted Avengers AI Labs database
an annotated dataset of 5 million frames collected on the battlefield

art.caption: Access is a training enclave. It is not a download of five million frames.
